classification.difficultyReason: Part (a) is easy. Part (b), the hardest, needs a quadratic or linear solve for V from a launch from height at 45°, then time of flight, final velocity components and impact angle. It is a longer chain of routine decisions with no new insight.

children.label: a
children.prompt: A stone is thrown horizontally from the top of a $45\text{ m}$ cliff and lands $60\text{ m}$ from the base of the cliff. Find the initial speed and the direction of motion when it lands, to the nearest degree.

answer.short: Initial speed $20\text{ m/s}$; $56^\circ$ below the horizontal.
answer.worked:
With the launch point as the origin, $\dot{x}=V$ and $\dot{y}=-10t$, so $x=Vt$ and $y=-5t^2$.

At landing, $y=-45$:
$$\begin{aligned}-45&=-5t^2\\t^2&=9\\t&=3\text{ s}\end{aligned}$$
Also $x=60$:
$$\begin{aligned}60&=3V\\V&=20\text{ m/s}\end{aligned}$$
At landing, $\dot{x}=20$ and $\dot{y}=-30$:
$$\begin{aligned}\tan\phi&=\frac{30}{20}\\\phi&=\tan^{-1}(1.5)\approx56^\circ\end{aligned}$$
The direction is $56^\circ$ below the horizontal.

children.label: b
children.prompt: A ball is thrown from the top of a $20\text{ m}$ building at an angle of $45^\circ$ above the horizontal. It lands $60\text{ m}$ from the base of the building. Find the initial speed to 1 d.p. and the direction of motion when it lands, to the nearest degree.

answer.short: Initial speed $\approx21.2\text{ m/s}$; $59^\circ$ below the horizontal.
answer.worked:
With the launch point as the origin, $\dot{x}=V\cos45^\circ$, $\dot{y}=-10t+V\sin45^\circ$, so $x=Vt\cos45^\circ$ and $y=-5t^2+Vt\sin45^\circ$.

Eliminating $t$ gives
$$y=x\tan45^\circ-\frac{5x^2}{V^2\cos^245^\circ}.$$
At landing, $x=60$ and $y=-20$:
$$\begin{aligned}-20&=60-\frac{5(3600)}{\frac12V^2}\\\frac{36000}{V^2}&=80\\V^2&=450\\V&=15\sqrt2\approx21.2\text{ m/s}\end{aligned}$$
Then $\dot{x}=V\cos45^\circ=15$, so
$$\begin{aligned}t&=\frac{60}{15}=4\text{ s}\\\dot{y}&=15-10(4)=-25\text{ m/s}\end{aligned}$$
If $\phi$ is the angle below the horizontal,
$$\begin{aligned}\tan\phi&=\frac{25}{15}\\\phi&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac53\right)\approx59^\circ\end{aligned}$$
The direction is $59^\circ$ below the horizontal.
